transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brought me in is that... some nights after work, or maybe after a tense dinner, I start eating and it just feels like the decision-making part of me shuts off completely. It's like I can physically see myself reaching for more food, but I just can't make myself stop.
After these episodes of eating, do you feel a need to do anything specific to make up for the amount you consumed, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

Yeah, I do. Um... there have been times, usually after everyone goes to bed, where I'll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up. Or sometimes I'll take laxatives. I just tell myself it’s a way to undo the damage from what I just ate. But honestly, right afterward... I just feel really embarrassed, and kind of physically shaky.
On average, how many times per week would you say these episodes of eating followed by purging occur?

Um, looking back over the last few months... I'd say it's been happening most weeks. Usually it's just one of those out-of-control eating nights a week, and then I try to make up for it. I'll do what I mentioned, throwing up or taking laxatives, but sometimes I'll also just skip meals the next day, or force myself to go on a really long walk.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a frequency of 'one' time per week for the past few months. According to DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria, Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2) requires a minimum frequency of once per week for 3 months, whereas Binge Eating Disorder (F50.3) does not involve regular purging behaviors. The presence of purging/compensatory behaviors shifts the diagnosis to F50.2.
